Paul — thanks for the clarifications and the questionnaire excerpt. Below is a consolidated, binding-leaning response you can share with procurement and privacy: please note where options exist (hosted vs dedicated/private) and the tradeoffs.

1) EU-only processing guarantee (hosted offering):
- Redwood Hosted (standard) offers region-restricted routing: customers may elect an EU-only processing policy. When enabled, inference, model serving, request logging, and ephemeral caches are routed to EEA regions only.
- Persistent artifacts (object storage, logs, backups) are placed in customer-configured EU buckets. By default we use the EEA cloud region corresponding to the account (Frankfurt/Paris/Amsterdam).
- Cross-border backups: our platform supports configurable backup targets. For customers requiring EU-only guarantees, we will configure backups to remain inside the EEA; we document the configuration and operational checklist in the SOW.

2) SCCs and transfer impact assessment (DTIA):
- Contractual: we offer the EU Commission SCCs via an EU Data Processing Addendum. We have an operational appendix describing subprocessors and data flows to demonstrate adherence.
- Technical: we provide our standard DTIA template that describes technical and organizational measures (encryption at rest/in transit, role-based access, logging, personnel access controls). We are prepared to provide the completed DTIA for Redwood Hosted for review during procurement.
- Support access: we minimize any non-EEA access by routing support sessions through EU-based engineers where possible; for exceptional cases (e.g., incident response requiring a specialist) we require prior customer consent and log/approve remote access. These exception processes are documented in the Addendum.

3) KMS / Encryption requirements:
- BYOK: we support customer-managed keys for object storage and snapshot encryption (via KMS integration). The KMS can be provisioned in the customer's EU tenant/region.

4) Retention and deletion:
- Retention windows are contractable per-data-class. Our default retention for logs is 90 days; we can extend to your 12-month requirement for conversational logs and 7 years for audit records via contractual configuration and billing adjustments.
- Deletion: we implement a multi-stage deletion flow: soft-delete -> retention tombstone -> physical purge. We provide deletion evidence (audit records) on request as part of incident/DSR workflows.

5) Private/Dedicated option (if you need stronger guarantees):
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity in EU) and Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) provide greater isolation. Private deployment allows full control of network egress and subprocessor list; if EuroFin needs absolute contractual assurance that no personnel outside the EEA may access data, Private is the recommended route.

6) Evidence and audits:
- We can provide SOC2 reports, subprocessor list, and a redacted evidence package for SCC review. For customers requiring on-site audits, we coordinate through our security team.

Attachments we've included for your review: redwood-eu-dataflow-v2.pdf (technical flow), SCCs-execution-steps.docx (contract steps and timelines).

- Rishi/Markus to propose a short technical session to review KMS and backup configuration.
- If EuroFin prefers, procurement can request our SOW for a Dedicated or Private deployment; that will include a detailed configuration and timeline.
